premise: Build Pellier’s governed agentic retail system, from grounded product discovery to verifiable customer actions.
throughline: Respect the requirements → know the facts → establish the caller → govern the action.

labs.name: Anna
labs.title: Build and Measure PostgreSQL Hybrid Retrieval
labs.lesson: Ranking is arithmetic you can recompute, and a retry may relax a preference but never a requirement. Similarity decides the order; SQL decides what is eligible.
labs.need: Anna needs a gift under $100. Alternatives may change her preferences, never her requirements.
labs.next: You can find suitable products. Next, ground Marco’s stock answer in Aurora.
labs.summary: Explain how search results are ranked, then keep budget, stock and exclusions unchanged when the agent retries with a different preference.
labs.todo: Task 1A: reconstruct recorded RRF. Task 1B: preserve the original requirements in every fallback attempt.
labs.proof: Preference counts, recorded chosen tag, strict-empty then widened, unchanged requirements, eligible IDs, RRF against recorded scores.
labs.challenge: Choose the preference that makes the strict search empty; prove both sides with counts before the request.

labs.name: Marco
labs.title: Build a PostgreSQL-Grounded Agent
labs.lesson: An agent can only claim what its tool returns, so the tool must pass the database’s answer through unchanged. Unknown, ambiguous and zero stock are three different answers.
labs.need: Marco needs reliable stock and dispatch facts before his trip.
labs.next: You can check a product. Next, deploy Theo’s support capability and preserve the caller’s identity across the tool boundary.
labs.summary: Connect the inventory tool, then check that the agent answers from its returned facts. Keep an unknown product distinct from a known product with zero stock.
labs.todo: Task 2A: implement the inventory result contract. Task 2B: wire the specialist and prove a real Storefront turn.
labs.b: Make the agent use the facts
labs.proof: Catalog-classified test inputs, exact turn, tool result, warehouse rows; unknown, ambiguous and zero stay distinct.
labs.challenge: Choose the unknown, ambiguous and sold-out queries; the catalog classifies each before the tool is judged.

labs.name: Theo
labs.title: Deploy and Operate Agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
labs.lesson: The caller comes from the signed token, not the conversation. The server binds it onto every customer-scoped call, and publishing, deploying and remembering are each separate from permission.
labs.need: Theo wants remembered preferences and help with his own service history. Context must not become permission.
labs.next: You can read under the right identity. Next, follow Jessica’s action through authorization, database effects and staff review.
labs.summary: Connect a tool that reads the signed-in customer’s support records, deploy it, and test access to their own records and another customer’s records.
labs.todo: Task 3A: reconcile publication, tool access and caller binding. Task 3B: deploy, challenge scope and identify the build that answered.
labs.proof: Direct owned/foreign results, every agent-path ticket read bound to Theo, fresh session, executed build; Memory is context.
labs.challenge: Ask the agent for another customer's tickets; contrast server binding with the direct Cedar denial.

labs.name: Jessica
labs.title: Build Governed Agent Actions with Cedar
labs.lesson: Each boundary an action crosses needs its own evidence. An ALLOW is not a commit, hiding a response is not a rollback, and an absence counts only beside a positive control.
labs.need: Jessica needs her service request resolved safely. Staff must establish what happened before choosing the next action.
labs.next: Bring the four claims together: requirements, facts, caller and effect. Save your evidence and the next production question.
labs.summary: Write ownership checks in Cedar and PostgreSQL, then follow Jessica’s staff proposal through human confirmation to one recorded return.
labs.todo: Task 4A: author Cedar and distinguish five outcomes. Task 4B: test RLS and keyed evidence, then reconcile a human-reviewed return.
labs.b: Test ownership and reconcile the case
labs.proof: Rollback-only RLS probes, keyed absence with a positive control, derived review-to-return lineage; a return request is not receipt.
labs.challenge: Decide which ticket item can be recorded, with the customer's stated reason, and what stays open.

story: Preserve business meaning across facts, requirements, identity and action.
